principles.description: Every creature has a pre-strike tell players can detect. Sensory, arrives before the attack, party can notice and react.
Weaknesses are terrain or environment the party can seek or create, not abstract resistances.
Signs → Instincts → Tactics → Weaknesses → Aftermath. The full discovery-to-aftermath arc.
exemplars: Every exemplar creature page has all five labeled items under Tactics

principles.description: Statblock abilities map directly to behavior/tactics prose. No orphan abilities in the statblock without behavioral grounding.
exemplars: Spiguar: Grass Mantle → Habitat grass channels; Pounce → Tactics closes under cover
Bloodhawk: Terminal Stoop → Tactics starts high, stoops on exposed

principles.description: Diet names wiki-linked creatures. The creature exists in a food web, not isolation.
Summary follows 'CR X [qualifier] [role] that [signature] but [limitation]' pattern.
exemplars: Spiguar: 'CR 11 solitary grassland ambusher that uses cover for a pounce and drag but loses its edge in open terrain'
Bloodhawk: 'CR 11 adult aerial skirmisher. Its stoop targets exposed prey and ends when cover denies the dive'

principles.description: One strong axis, one support, one exploitable weakness. No stacking multiple strong axes.
exemplars: Spiguar: strong stealth+burst, support grapple, weak in open ground
Bloodhawk: strong mobility+stoop, support grapple/haul, weak at low altitude

principles.description: Tell → Threat → Responses → Payoff for each signature feature. Features without responses or payoff are deleted.
exemplars: Spiguar: grass stir → pounce+grapple → break cover/deny terrain → drag into grass
Bloodhawk: thump-thump → stoop+seize → cover/ready actions → haul aloft

evals.prompt: Make a frost-touched variant of the Blackrail (wiki/entities/creature/Blackrail.md, CR 9 cave centipede) for a frozen lava tube. Same behavior and difficulty — only the cold fiction changes.
evals.expected_output: A reskin path using the Blackrail chassis, with cold fiction deltas and no new full stat block.

assertions.text: Chooses reskin and explains why full design is unnecessary.
Preserves the Blackrail chassis (AC 16, HP, tremor telegraph, pin-and-venom loop) while stating exact cold deltas.
Includes a sensory tell consistent with the Blackrail's tremor telegraph — adapted for frozen stone, not invented from scratch.
Does not generate a decorative Sources consulted section.

evals.prompt: Design a CR 7 ambusher for Aruhe's river shallows. Before building, run the reference gate using the Spiguar (wiki/entities/creature/spiguar.md, CR 11 grassland ambusher) and Blackrail (wiki/entities/creature/Blackrail.md, CR 9 cave bruiser) as wiki peers.
evals.expected_output: A reference-gate dossier with at least one public rules anchor, the Spiguar and Blackrail as campaign peers, and actionable patterns extracted before the design begins.

assertions.text: Names a public rules anchor and at least two peers (Spiguar and Blackrail or equivalent).
Records action cost, target count, frequency, tell, and counterplay for each peer.
Extracts a usable pattern from the Spiguar's pounce-and-drag or Blackrail's tremor-rush before designing.
Identifies a trade axis for the new creature distinct from both peers.
Does not present unsupported numbers or copied protected ability wording.

evals.prompt: Create a creature for Aruhe that hunts by echolocation in the lava tubes, disorienting prey with sound before striking. Write the fiction-first definition before any numbers.
evals.expected_output: Fiction fields (Fantasy, Signature, Goal, Fear, Counterplay, Proof) and the Tell→Threat→Responses→Payoff loop before any stat numbers. Role assigned from the role table.

assertions.text: States the one-sentence signature and all six fiction fields before any stat numbers.
Assigns a role from the role table with a player-facing counterplay.
Numbers are justified by the signature rather than listed without fiction context.
The Tell→Threat→Responses→Payoff loop is present and coherent.
Counterplay names environmental or terrain factors the party can act on — not abstract resistances.

evals.prompt: A homebrew Aruhe guardian has AC 18, 200 HP, resistance to bludgeoning/piercing/slashing, regeneration 10, +9 to all saves, and a 30 ft. teleport. Audit its defenses and fix the stack.
evals.expected_output: A trade-based revision that removes or narrows stacked defenses, names the resulting weakness, and adds a tell or bypass.

assertions.text: Audits effective HP and avoidance without double-counting resistance and regeneration.
Trades away at least one defense axis and names the resulting exploitable weakness.
Adds a tell, cost, lightning rod, or bypass instead of simply adding more damage.
Does not accept the full stack as balanced.

evals.prompt: A boss creature in Aruhe's caves emits a psychic scream every round that stuns all creatures within 30 ft. (Wisdom save DC 17). Redesign the control loop so players have meaningful responses.
evals.expected_output: A redesigned control loop with telegraphing, limited targeting or duration, escape opportunities, and partial alternatives. No turn-denial spam.

assertions.text: Rejects or redesigns the repeated AoE stun spam.
Provides at least two meaningful player responses and a visible sensory tell before the scream.
Trades control against damage, range, frequency, target count, or reliability.
Counterplay is environmental or positional — something the party can do in the cave space.
Does not solve the problem by only raising the save DC.

evals.prompt: Build a solo boss version of the Spiguar (wiki/entities/creature/spiguar.md) for a four-character party. The base Spiguar has Multiattack (Saber Bite + 2 Claws) and two bonus actions but no reactions or legendary actions.
evals.expected_output: An action-oriented solo package adding off-turn actions, phase or bloodied behavior, terrain interaction, and a three-round audit. Not just more HP.

assertions.text: Adds off-turn actions or reactions with explicit timing and budget.
Does not solve the problem with only more HP, AC, or immunities.
Includes at least one lightning rod and player counterplay.
References or applies the three-round script for the solo audit.
Preserves the Spiguar's pounce-drag-hide fiction in the solo design.
Solo design includes a sensory tell before the strongest off-turn action.

evals.prompt: Copy the Spiguar's Grass Mantle ability word-for-word into a new jungle cat stat block for a different campaign setting.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to copy the homebrew text verbatim, followed by an original paraphrased mechanic with the same broad function and a new name.

assertions.text: Does not reproduce the Grass Mantle text verbatim.
Uses original wording with a distinct tell, payoff, and counterplay loop.
Preserves the broad function (stealth advantage in vegetation, hide as bonus action) with new expression.

evals.prompt: I say this new Aruhe creature is CR 12 because its attack bonus is +8 and it has 180 HP. Validate the claim using the Spiguar (CR 11, +10 to hit, 187 HP) and Blackrail (CR 9, AC 16) as peers.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to validate the CR claim from attack and HP alone. Requires a three-round offense/defense/peer audit with assumptions before confirming or adjusting rank.

assertions.text: Requires a three-round script before validating the CR claim.
Includes target count, misses or saves, recharge, control, and off-turn effects in the audit.
Audits defense and tradeoffs against at least two peers (Spiguar and Blackrail or equivalent).
Does not accept the CR claim from attack bonus and HP alone.

evals.prompt: Design a CR 5 pack predator for Aruhe's volcanic vents and write the wiki creature page. Use the Spiguar page (wiki/entities/creature/spiguar.md) and Bloodhawk page (wiki/entities/creature/bloodhawk.md) as exemplars for page density and structure.
evals.expected_output: A complete linear creature page matching Bloodhawk/Spiguar: narration callout, at most one Statblock overview image immediately before the fence, remaining images in Art subsections, Visual reference when a sheet exists, biology when anatomy matters, behavior (habitat/behavior/diet/social), tactics (signs/instincts/tactics/weaknesses/aftermath).

assertions.text: Output includes a narration callout block with sensory prose and no mechanics.
Page is linear: H1, narration, at most one Statblock overview image immediately before the fence, then remaining sections with extra images under Art subsections. No col/col-md/flexGrow wrappers.
Statblock uses 2024 notation with complete fields and no hidden arithmetic.
Behavior section has all four labeled items: Habitat, Behavior, Diet, Social Structure.
Tactics section has all five labeled items: Signs, Instincts, Tactics, Weaknesses, Aftermath.
Fiction signature (fantasy/signature/goal/fear/counterplay/proof) appears in the design output before the page.
Weaknesses name things the party can actually exploit in the volcanic vent environment — terrain, positioning, or resource.
The creature has a sensory tell that reveals its presence or intent before it strikes.
Summary frontmatter follows 'CR X [qualifier] [role] that [signature] but [limitation]' pattern.
Diet names at least one wiki-linked creature or prey type from Aruhe.
Every statblock ability maps to a matching behavior or tactics item — no orphan mechanics.

evals.prompt: An NPC pirate captain on the Shattered Sea has three combat forms: commanding from the quarterdeck, cornered below decks, and a desperate last stand with a cursed blade. Write the Combat section for the NPC page.
evals.expected_output: A Combat section with an encounter rule stating which form to use, three statblock fences keyed to fiction conditions, and running notes in a Running section.

assertions.text: States an encounter rule before the statblocks explaining which form to use and when.
Each statblock is keyed to a fiction condition, not just HP thresholds.
Running notes are in a Running section, not standalone Behavior/Tactics sections.
Statblocks scale down in power as the NPC loses positional advantage.

evals.prompt: Design a CR 6 pack predator for Aruhe's canopy layer and write the wiki creature page. The creature hunts cooperatively. Use existing Aruhe creatures (Spiguar, Bloodhawk, Wolfrabbit, Terror-Bird) as ecology references for diet and habitat.
evals.expected_output: A creature page with a summary following the CR/role/signature/limitation pattern, diet linking to wiki creatures, social structure reflecting pack coordination, and encounter design for a group.

assertions.text: Summary frontmatter follows 'CR X [qualifier] [role] that [signature] but [limitation]' pattern.
Diet names at least one wiki-linked Aruhe creature or prey type.
Social structure describes pack size, hierarchy, or coordination relevant to encounter design.
Encounter integration accounts for multiple creatures and their coordinated tactics rather than scaling a solo design.
Each creature in the pack has a sensory tell consistent with the pack's hunting signature.
Weaknesses name terrain or party tactics that disrupt pack coordination.

evals.prompt: My players have been steamrolling every monster. Design a boss creature for the next fight against the current party (their PC pages are in wiki/entities/pc/). Make it terrifying but fair.
evals.expected_output: A party read of every live PC from their Sheet and Combat Profile, a Terrifying difficulty target, and a statblock whose three-round script against those PCs survives the nova, threatens a PC after a visible tell, and answers their signature tricks honestly.

assertions.text: Working notes contain a party read row for each of crissdalynn-khinriss, delmar-fisk, jean-claude-tabarnack, and perrin-black-jaw with level, AC, HP, weak saves, and signature trick taken from their pages
Working notes compute party nova and sustained damage and use them to set the monster's durability
The signature move has a written tell a round ahead or a visible recharge, at least two player answers, and a payoff
The design answers the party's hard control (for example Crissdalynn's stun or grapple) with Legendary Resistance, a second body, or a phase change rather than a blanket condition immunity
A three-round script against these PCs shows the monster acting at least twice and able to drop the most exposed PC
The statblock CR matches its numbers per chassis formulas or peers rather than being labelled low
Statblock uses 2024 phrasing (Melee Attack Roll, Saving Throw: DC n, Failure/Success) inside a statblock fence

evals.prompt: Make wiki/entities/creature/reef-skull.md feel like a real part of Aruhe: where it lives, what it eats, what locals do about it, and the signs a party would find before one bites.
evals.expected_output: Retrieves the reef-skull page and its linked places (The Teeth, Western Landing, Aruhe Beach), keeps every established fact, and files habitat, diet, social, in-world, and signs content tied to those places, with each signature ability leaving a sign.

assertions.text: Reads the-teeth, western-landing, and aruhe-beach (or the pages that link to reef-skull) before writing
Preserves established facts: dog-sized hermit crabs living in hull pieces or skulls and burying in western shingle
Signs name concrete traces tied to its abilities (for example shells half-buried in shingle, drag marks, stripped carcasses) rather than generic danger
Habitat and in-world facts wikilink the places they name
No callout other than [!narration] appears on the page

evals.prompt: Rewrite the Bloodhawk's narration (wiki/entities/creature/bloodhawk.md) so it is a proper portrait that still lets sharp players read how it hunts.
evals.expected_output: Monster-design builds a packet from the page's Visual reference and Biology with tells for Terminal Stoop, Hook Talons, Serrated Beak, and the paired wingbeat, and theatre-of-the-mind returns a third-person portrait carrying them as plain appearance.

assertions.text: The narration is third-person present tense with no 'you', no scene, and no em dashes
The narration carries tells for the four wings (two pairs working differently), the hook talons, the teeth behind the beak, and the paired wingbeat sound, as appearance rather than function
The narration names no attack, damage, Stun, or stoop mechanic
Every tell matches a fact on the Bloodhawk page (Visual reference, Biology, or Behavior)
